text: 🇲🇽🔬 "It sometimes sounds very difficult for us to become a scientific and technological power, but we have everything to do it." — Rosaura Ruiz, Secretary of Science, Humanities, Technology and Innovation In 2026, research projects received 1,676 million pesos more than in 2025. Approved projects rose 48%, there are more than 100,000 graduate scholarships, and public research centers received 200 new positions, their first real expansion since most were founded in the 1970s. Strategic projects include Olinia (Mexican electric mini-vehicle), Kutsari (semiconductors), Coatlicue (Latin America's most powerful supercomputer) and an Earth-observation satellite constellation.

🇲🇽💵 <u>Remittances Dip in August, Still Up 2.2% for the Year</u>

Mexico received $5.452 billion in remittances in August, down 3.6% year on year, which ends a six-month growth streak, El Financiero reports from Banxico data. The number of transfers fell 6.4% to 13.24 million, but the average transfer rose 3% to $412.

January through August, migrant families sent home $41.8 billion, up 2.2%. Under ICE raids and Trump's remittance tax, Mexicans abroad are sending less often but sending more each time.

🇲🇽🔬 <u>Mexico's Science Fund Jumps 111%</u>

Secihti chief Rosaura Ruiz reported during the review of Sheinbaum's Second Report that research, development and innovation projects have an extra 1.676 billion pesos in 2026, a 111% increase over 2025. That money funds 1,340 new technology and innovation projects, and 44.7% of their lead investigators are women.

The fund also supports 3,142 ongoing research projects, more than 100,000 graduate scholarships and 13 national strategic projects. The neoliberal decades starved Conacyt. This government is funding science.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>AMLO Returns: Fobaproa Will Cost Mexico 8.4 Trillion Pesos</u>

Reappearing in a video message to present his new book "Pueblo," López Obrador put a final price on Zedillo's bank bailout: 8.4 trillion pesos by the time it's paid off, "until 2050, if things go well." So far 1.6 trillion pesos have gone to interest alone, and the principal hasn't moved.

He reminded viewers who brokered it: the PRI and the PAN, with Felipe Calderón negotiating for Acción Nacional. He also noted that under Calderón and Peña Nieto, 50 big corporations got 300 billion pesos in tax forgiveness. That ended with his constitutional reform to Article 28.

🇲🇽🛢️ <u>Pemex Crude Exports Plunge 44.8% as Mexico Refines at Home</u>

Pemex shipped just 275,737 barrels a day of crude abroad in August, down 44.8% from a year earlier and 39% from July, according to La Jornada. Revenue from foreign crude sales fell 34.3% to $626.9 million.

The barrels aren't vanishing. They're going into Mexican refineries, which raised gasoline and diesel output the same month. For decades Mexico sold crude cheap and bought back fuel dear. That trade is now being reversed.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>Sheinbaum to Washington: Revoke Asylum for the Ayotzinapa Judge</u>

President Sheinbaum is demanding the US withdraw asylum from José Ulises Bernabé García, the on-duty Iguala barandilla judge the night 43 Ayotzinapa students were disappeared in 2014. He fled north in 2015, claimed "persecution," and the US Justice Department granted him protection in 2020 — while Mexico seeks his extradition.

Mexico has handed Washington dozens of cartel figures it wanted. Sheinbaum's demand is reciprocity: "You cannot be asking on one side and not responding on the other."

🇲🇽🌾 <u>Michoacán wheat: 7,600 pesos a ton vs 4,600 on the market</u>

Federal guaranteed prices for small and medium producers in Michoacán run from 7,050 to 9,080 pesos per ton (El Economista). Small wheat farmers get 7,600 pesos, plus a 200-peso climate incentive, against an average rural price of about 4,600. Small rice growers get 9,080 against about 5,800. That's roughly 3,000 extra pesos a ton for the smallest wheat farms, across 27,284 hectares in 54 municipalities.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>Mexico and Canada deepen intelligence and cybersecurity ties</u>

Security chief Omar García Harfuch met the Business Council of Canada, led by Goldy Hyder, and announced broader binational cooperation on intelligence and cybersecurity, where information-sharing is key. The Canadian side acknowledged the results of Sheinbaum's security strategy and the SSPC's work strengthening intelligence and investigation.
